new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: group-level-statement. Mirror snippet extract lines 7-19: Laycock's remark 'Stress does not appear to be a phonemic feature in any of these languages' covers the whole Lumi survey (c. 50 lists), and 'Stress is marked only if it falls on other than the first syllable not containing [schwa]' is a marking convention. The 'weight-sensitive' reading was built by the finder from the absence of marks on the 46 Seti forms in TransNewGuinea.org's re-keying (original table not seen); as text the quotation states nothing Seti-specific, so record survey-level 'non-phonemic, default first full-vowel syllable' and leave the type unclear until the OL table is seen. | checker: Crossref 10.…
new_statements.relation_note: Non-phonemic stress in all surveyed languages; default position first non-schwa syllable; nothing on tone in the snippets seen.
new_statements.rule_in_words: For all Lumi-area languages surveyed (Seti = list 3) stress is judged non-phonemic; Laycock's default, left unmarked, is stress on the first syllable whose vowel is not [ə], and he marks stress only where it falls elsewhere. TransNewGuinea's re-keying of his lists preserves his acute marks for other languages (Seta kamóya, Elkei nuŋáwo) and shows none on any of the 46 Seti forms, so every recorded Seti word follows the default (e.g. ko:liyo -> KO:liyo, pənanuwi -> pəNAnuwi, təmpofənə -> təmPOfənə). Equivalent label: initial stress skipping schwa syllables (quality-sensitive, left-edge).
new_statements.exceptions: Forms stressed elsewhere are individually marked in the lists; none of the Seti forms is marked (per TransNewGuinea re-keying; original table not seen).
new_statements.identity_note: Seti is Laycock's language no. 3 'Seti (Aunalei)', village Mauwil (W. Wapei CD), informant Wop, elicited Lumi June 1967 = the DCL67 test list that Laycock 1973 and Glottolog attach to seti1248. The stress sentence is a general statement over all the languages whose wordlists the article publishes (Seti included), not a Seti-specific paragraph; the Seti entry itself has no '(e) phonemes' note.
